en: And Umayyah ibn Bistam narrated to me: Yazid—meaning Ibn Zuray'—narrated to us (H). And Ali ibn Hujr narrated to me: Ismail—meaning Ibn Ulayyah—narrated to us; both from Rawh ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, the like of the hadith of Ibn Uyaynah, except that he did not mention: "nor will we please your eye with it."

Amr al-Naqid and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr both narrated to us from Sufyan; Amr said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us: Ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: A boy was born to a man among us, and he named him al-Qasim. We said: "We will not call you Abu al-Qasim, nor will we please your eye with it." So he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Name your son Abd al-Rahman."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Mansur (H). And Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Jabalah narrated to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us (H). And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us; both from Shu'bah, from Husayn (H). And Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—informed us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman; all of them from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, they said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, Mansur, Sulayman, and Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman; they said: We heard Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of those whose narration we mentioned before. And in the hadith of al-Nadr from Shu'bah, he said: Husayn and Sulayman added to it: Husayn said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I was only sent as a distributor (Qasim) to divide among you." And Sulayman said: "For I am only a distributor (Qasim) dividing among you."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Qatadah, from Salim, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that a boy was born to a man from the Ansar and he wanted to name him Muhammad. So he came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and asked him, and he said: "The Ansar have done well. Name with my name, but do not take my kunyah."
And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, and he said: "I was only made a distributor (Qasim) dividing among you."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash (H). And Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to me: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah, for I am Abu al-Qasim, dividing among you." And in the narration of Abu Bakr: "and do not take my kunyah (la taktatu)."

Rifa'ah ibn al-Haytham al-Wasiti narrated to us: Khalid—meaning al-Tahhan—narrated to us, from Husayn, with this chain of narration, and he did not mention: "For I was only sent as a distributor dividing among you."

Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Abthar narrated to us, from Husayn, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: A boy was born to a man among us, and he named him Muhammad. We said: "We will not call you by the kunyah of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) until you consult him." He said: So he went to him and said: "A boy was born to me, and I named him after the Messenger of Allah, but my people refused to call me by his kunyah until you ask permission of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." He said: "Name with my name, but do not take my kunyah, for I was only sent as a distributor dividing among you."

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Uthman said: narrated to us, and Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: A boy was born to a man among us, and he named him Muhammad. His people said to him: "We will not let you name him with the name of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." So he set off with his son carrying him on his back, and brought him to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a boy was born to me and I named him Muhammad, but my people said to me: We will not let you name him with the name of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah, for I am only a distributor dividing among you."

Ibrahim ibn Ziyad—who is surnamed Sabalan—narrated to me: Abbad ibn Abbad informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar and his brother Abd Allah—he heard it from both of them in the year one hundred and forty-four, narrating from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, the dearest of your names to Allah are Abd Allah and Abd al-Rahman."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala' and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to me—Abu Kurayb said: informed us, and Ibn Abi Umar said: narrated to us, and the wording is his; they said: Marwan—meaning al-Fazari—narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: A man called out to another man in al-Baqi': "O Abu al-Qasim!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) turned toward him. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not mean you; I only called so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not take my kunyah."
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us; both from Hisham, with this chain of narration.

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abdah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from Fatimah, from Asma': A woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "I have a co-wife; is there any sin upon me if I pretend to have received from my husband's property what he did not give me?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The one who pretends to have received what they were not given is like the wearer of two garments of falsehood."

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki' and Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, that a woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, I claim that my husband gave me what he did not give me." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The one who pretends to have received what they were not given is like the wearer of two garments of falsehood."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There are two types among the people of the Fire whom I have not seen: people having whips like the tails of cattle with which they strike people, and women who are clothed yet naked, enticing others and walking with an enticing gait, with their heads like the humps of slanted Bactrian camels. They will not enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance, even though its fragrance can be perceived from such-and-such a distance."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There are two types among the people of the Fire whom I have not seen: people having whips like the tails of cattle with which they strike people, and women who are clothed yet naked, enticing others and walking with an enticing gait, with their heads like the humps of slanted Bactrian camels. They will not enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance, even though its fragrance can be perceived from such-and-such a distance."

And Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, they said: Mu'adh—namely Ibn Hisham—informed us: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Mu'awiyah said one day: "You have introduced an evil fashion, and the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade falsehood." He said: And a man came with a staff on top of which was a piece of cloth. Mu'awiyah said: "Behold, this too is falsehood." Qatadah said: "Meaning what women use to make their hair look thicker using pieces of cloth."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah (H). And Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Mu'awiyah came to Medina and delivered a sermon to us, and he took out a ball of hair and said: "I did not think anyone would do this except the Jews. When it reached the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he called it falsehood."

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us (H). And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me (H). And Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; all of them from al-Zuhri, the like of the hadith of Malik, except that in the hadith of Ma'mar: "The Children of Israel were only punished..."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, that he heard Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan in the year he performed Hajj, while on the pulpit, take a tuft of hair that was in the hand of a guard, saying: "O people of Medina, where are your scholars? I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbid the like of this, saying: The Children of Israel only perished when their women adopted this."

And al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hulwani and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) reprimanded that a woman should attach anything to her head.

And Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir—meaning Ibn Hazim—narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to their hadith.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, with this chain of narration: the hadith from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) alone, without the rest of the story mentioning Umm Ya'qub.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Abd al-Rahman—namely Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Mufaddal—namely Ibn Muhalhal—narrated to us; both from Mansur in this chain of narration, in the meaning of the hadith of Jarir, except that in the hadith of Sufyan it is "the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed (al-washimat wal-mustawshimat)," and in the hadith of Mufaddal it is "the women who tattoo and those who are tattooed (al-washimat wal-mawshumat)."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is Ishaq's: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: May Allah curse the women who practice tattooing and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck eyebrows and those who have their eyebrows plucked, and those who make spaces between their teeth for beauty, altering the creation of Allah. He said: That reached a woman of Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, who used to recite the Quran. She came to him and said: "What is this hadith that has reached me from you, that you curse the women who practice tattooing and those who have themselves tattooed, those who have their eyebrows plucked, and those who make spaces between their teeth for beauty, altering the creation of Allah?" Abd Allah said: "Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cursed, and it is in the Book of Allah?" The woman said: "I have read what is between the two covers of the Mushaf, and I did not find it." He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, leave it}." The woman said: "Indeed, I see some of this on your own wife right now." He said: "Go and look." He said: So she entered upon Abd Allah's wife and did not see anything. She came back to him and said: "I did not see anything." He said: "Indeed, if that were the case, we would not live with her."

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us (H). And Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's; both said: Yahya—namely al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cursed the woman who adds hair extensions and the woman who asks for them, and the woman who tattoos and the woman who asks to be tattooed. And Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated it to me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Abd Allah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Nafi': al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannaq informed me, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from Aisha, that a woman from the Ansar married off a daughter of hers, but she fell ill and her hair fell out. She came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Her husband desires her; may I attach extensions to her hair?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Cursed are the women who add hair extensions." And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Nafi', with this chain of narration, and he said: "Cursed are the women who attach hair extensions."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Abu Dawud narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us (H). And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard al-Hasan ibn Muslim narrating from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, from Aisha, that a young girl from the Ansar got married and fell ill so that her hair fell out. They wanted to add hair extensions to it, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about that, and he cursed the woman who adds hair extensions and the woman who asks for them.

And Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi narrated to me: Habban informed us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Mansur narrated to us, from his mother, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, that a woman came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "I married off my daughter and the hair of her head fell out, while her husband finds her attractive; may I attach extensions to it, O Messenger of Allah?" So he forbade her.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us: Abdah narrated to us (H). And Ibn Numayr narrated it to us: My father and Abdah narrated to us (H). And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us (H). And Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Aswad ibn Amir informed us: Shu'bah informed us; all of them from Hisham ibn Urwah, with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, except that in the hadith of the two it says: "so her hair fell out."
